classification.difficultyReason: Select differences of basic circular/rectangular areas across ten supplied figures, infer diameter by familiar Pythagoras in three parts and add three semicircles in one part.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of the shaded region in each diagram. Give exact answers and approximations correct to 2 decimal places where needed.

answer.worked:
The rectangle diagonal is a diameter of its circumcircle.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=5^2+5^2=50\\r^2&=d^2/4=25/2\\A&=\pi(25/2)-25\\A&=\tfrac{25}{2}\pi-25\text{ cm}^2\approx14.27\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
The rectangle diagonal is a diameter of its circumcircle.
$$\begin{aligned}d^2&=12^2+5^2=169\\r^2&=169/4\\A&=169\pi/4-12(5)\\A&=\tfrac{169}{4}\pi-60\text{ cm}^2\approx72.73\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Cyclic kite with two equal3 sides and two equal4 sides, diagonal5. Both 3-4-5 triangles have hypotenusePQ diameter5; source top/bottom matching families retained; no added rightangle given.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens only; no derived radius or area given in diagram.

answer.worked:
The equal-side marks give two congruent 3–4–5 right triangles; their common hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle.
$$\begin{aligned}3^2+4^2&=5^2\\A_{\text{kite}}&=2(\tfrac12)(3)(4)=12\\r&=5/2\\A&=25\pi/4-12\\A&=\tfrac{25}{4}\pi-12\text{ cm}^2\approx7.63\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
